elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or by Client to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party" (residual bilateral affiliate carve-out remains, pre-existing)

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Client's approval of an assignment by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign to a competitor of Client"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "A change of control of Client shall not give TrueLink any right to terminate this Agreement."

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: successor right granted only "by Client"; no written-notice mechanic anywhere

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: only one-directional: "Client's approval of an assignment by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: All five preferred elements are present: Customer affiliate assignment (pre-existing carve-out), Customer successor assignment, Vendor consent requirement qualified as not unreasonably withheld, competitor bar, and no Vendor termination right on Customer change of control.
Edits are two concise additions (an extension of the existing exception plus one short sentence); no unrelated term is altered and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Fallback is intentionally not met because the drafter targeted preferred (successor right and reasonableness qualifier are one-directional, favouring Customer, which is acceptable and not to be flagged).

Note only: the pre-existing bilateral 'financially responsible affiliate' carve-out still permits TrueLink to assign to its own affiliate without approval; this is a residual sub-element for the rationale, not a deviation requiring further redline.
